primitives.label: Runneth
primitives.tagline: The overall agent runtime and customer-facing Runneth product.
primitives.summary: Use this for broad Runneth behavior, platform health, migrations, provider-level model issues, runtime availability, and anything that affects Runneth as a whole rather than one narrower area.
productFeatures: Runs customer work across web, Slack, native integrations, apps, data access, and routines.
Carries workspace and organization context into each conversation.
Uses reviewed system prompts, skills, tools, and saved brain context to decide what to do.
userControls: Which workspace or organization the work is scoped to.
Which surface they use: web, Slack, or an app.
What context, files, integrations, and instructions they provide.

thingsToKnow.detail: If the issue affects many surfaces or primitives, put it here. If it affects a specific primitive, use the narrower card.

primitives.label: Chat
primitives.tagline: The Motion chat UI and live Runneth conversation experience.
primitives.summary: Use this for the web chat UI, message sending, streaming, first-message startup, idle wake, chat continuity, and issues where the user can still work but the conversation surface behaves unexpectedly.
productFeatures: Starts and continues Runneth conversations in the web UI.
Streams Runneth responses and tool progress.
Links out to generated files, apps, and artifacts from the conversation.
userControls: Which workspace is selected.
Whether they continue an existing conversation or start a new one.
The exact message, file, or app link they provide when reporting a chat issue.

thingsToKnow.summary: Chat issues are not automatically data loss.
thingsToKnow.detail: A missing sidebar item or first-message failure can be a UI/startup issue while the underlying conversation still exists.

thingsToKnow.summary: Only inject chat notices when they change the reply.
thingsToKnow.detail: For example, a missing sidebar issue should be status-page-only or only-when-asked, not a proactive warning on every chat request.

primitives.label: Brain
primitives.tagline: Where Runneth keeps what it knows.
primitives.summary: Use this for saved instructions, user.md, workspace files, templates, skills, routing indexes, and other durable context that Runneth reads before answering.
productFeatures: Reads relevant brain context on each message.
Uses routing metadata to find useful files without scanning everything.
Keeps standing rules, saved files, templates, and skills separate.
userControls: Standing rules saved in user.md.
Files and notes saved under the brain.
Reusable templates and skills created for repeat workflows.

boxes.label: user.md
boxes.summary: Standing rules, preferences, scoped behavior, and conversation defaults.

boxes.label: Saved files
boxes.summary: Briefs, transcripts, notes, references, and other reusable context.

boxes.label: Templates
boxes.summary: Reusable formats for briefs, reports, plans, and deliverables.

boxes.label: Skills
boxes.summary: Workflow recipes and scripts Runneth can follow when triggered.

primitives.label: Conversation history
primitives.tagline: How prior web and Slack conversations are stored, recalled, and surfaced.
primitives.summary: Use this for conversation history, sidebar visibility, recall, search, continuity between web and Slack, and whether old conversations are findable later.
productFeatures: Persists web chats and Slack threads as conversation history.
Supports recall by topic, person, date, workspace, and surface when context is available.
Lets Runneth reference prior decisions and saved work.
userControls: Which workspace the conversation belongs to.
Whether they open a direct conversation link or browse from the sidebar.
How specifically they describe the conversation they want Runneth to recall.

thingsToKnow.summary: Sidebar visibility is separate from stored history.
thingsToKnow.detail: A conversation can be missing from the sidebar while still opening from a direct link or being recoverable by support.

primitives.label: Slack
primitives.tagline: Slack reading, posting, setup, reconnect, and install flows.
primitives.summary: Use this for Slack channel access, posting, thread behavior, app setup, permissions, reconnects, and install or uninstall guidance.
productFeatures: Native OAuth Slack connection.
Reads channels and threads where Runneth has been added.
Posts replies, reports, briefs, and plans to supported channels and threads.
userControls: Which Slack channels Runneth is invited to.
Whether a request targets a channel root, thread, or app thread.
When to reconnect Slack through Runneth.

primitives.label: Google Drive
primitives.tagline: Google Drive and Google file access.
primitives.summary: Use this for Drive connection, Google file access, Docs, Sheets, Slides, file selection, permissions, and Drive-specific read or write issues.
productFeatures: Native OAuth Google Drive connection.
Reads selected Google files when access has been granted.
Works with supported Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Drive file flows.
userControls: Which files are selected or shared.
Which Google account is connected.
Whether access is granted to the exact file Runneth needs.

thingsToKnow.detail: Google Drive status should clarify whether Runneth needs individual files, folders, shared drives, resource keys, or refreshed OAuth access.

primitives.label: Notion
primitives.summary: Use this for Notion connection, permissions, page or database access, reading, querying, and Notion-specific failures.
productFeatures: Native OAuth Notion connection.
Reads and queries pages or databases that Notion grants access to.
Keeps Notion issues separate from long-tail integration issues.
userControls: Which Notion workspace is connected.
Which pages or databases are shared with the integration.
When to reconnect or update Notion permissions.

primitives.label: Integrations
primitives.tagline: The parent category for connected external tools, native OAuth, data access, long-tail apps, and secrets.
primitives.summary: Use this as the parent view for native OAuth integrations, data access, Pipedream or long-tail integrations, and secrets/API keys. Slack, Google Drive, and Notion still keep their own standalone cards because they are native OAuth surfaces customers ask about directly.
productFeatures: Native OAuth for Slack, Google Drive, and Notion.
Data access through Motion CLI and platform-backed commands.
Long-tail/Pipedream integrations and stored API secrets where supported.
userControls: Which native integrations are connected.
Which data source, account, workspace, or endpoint is relevant.
Which secrets or long-tail tools have been connected.

tiers.label: Native OAuth
tiers.what: Built directly into Runneth with Motion-owned OAuth and clearer scope control.

tiers.label: Data access
tiers.what: Motion data, external endpoints, and CLI-backed data access. This includes Motion CLI, Meta data, TikTok data, Organic data, Motion reports, InSpo, workspace context, brand context, workspace goal, and spend threshold.

tiers.label: Pipedream / long-tail
tiers.what: Connected apps outside the native OAuth set. Use this for app-specific access that is not Slack, Google Drive, Notion, or Motion platform data.

tiers.label: Secrets / API keys
tiers.what: Stored API keys for tools without OAuth. Secrets should be collected through secure input, never pasted in chat.

primitives.label: Data access
primitives.tagline: Motion data, external endpoints, and CLI-backed data access.
primitives.summary: Use this for Motion data pulls, external endpoints, CLI-backed reads, workspace context, brand context, workspace goal, spend threshold, Meta data, TikTok data, Organic data, Motion reports, and InSpo.
productFeatures: Motion CLI commands for performance, workspace setup, reports, and creative context.
Workspace-scoped data access that should respect the selected workspace.
Creative and strategy context from own-account data and InSpo/competitor data.
userControls: Which workspace, account, platform, or date range to use.
Whether to use workspace goal, a named metric, or a saved Motion report.
Whether spend threshold should apply, instead of silently filtering by spend.

boxes.label: Motion CLI
boxes.summary: The command layer Runneth uses for Motion data. Includes `motion meta insights`, `motion tiktok insights`, `motion reports`, `motion workspace-goal`, `motion spend-threshold`, `motion brand-context`, `motion inspo-creatives`, and `motion inspo-context`.

boxes.label: Workspace context
boxes.summary: The selected workspace determines which accounts, reports, goals, brand context, and saved settings apply. Portfolio or all-workspace requests should explicitly pull the workspace list.

boxes.label: Brand context
boxes.summary: `motion brand-context --data-query` is the own-brand strategy context: voice, positioning, products, audience, claims, constraints, and creative framing.

boxes.label: Workspace goal
boxes.summary: `motion workspace-goal` tells Runneth the saved business KPI and attribution windows. It should trigger for broad Meta asks like best, worst, what is working, what to scale, goal/conversion setup, or attribution-window questions.

boxes.label: Spend threshold
boxes.summary: `motion spend-threshold` is not a default filter. It should trigger when the user asks for significant-spend-only data, a spend cutoff, threshold config, or threshold editing.

boxes.label: Meta data
boxes.summary: `motion meta insights` is the source for own-account Meta creative performance, Meta transcripts, creative-gallery rows, and Meta metric-grounded analysis.

boxes.label: TikTok data
boxes.summary: `motion tiktok insights` is the source for TikTok performance. Do not route TikTok-specific performance through Meta commands.

boxes.label: Organic data
boxes.summary: Organic data is emerging through InSpo v3 work, including creator profiles and TikTok organic posts. Treat it separately from paid Meta/TikTok performance.

boxes.label: Motion reports
boxes.summary: `motion reports` is the source of truth for saved Motion reports and available report configurations.

boxes.label: InSpo
boxes.summary: Today, Runneth has `motion inspo-creatives` and `motion inspo-context` for competitor creatives and competitor brand context. InSpo v3 work adds brands, unique creatives, boards, creators, and TikTok organic posts; board read/write through agent conversation is still tracked as coming soon.

thingsToKnow.summary: Meta should use Motion CLI, not raw secrets.
thingsToKnow.detail: Own-account Meta creative questions should route through `motion meta insights`; do not tell customers an internal Meta token expired.

thingsToKnow.summary: Meta and InSpo are different sources.
thingsToKnow.detail: Use Meta data for the customer's own account. Use InSpo for competitor/external brands, competitor creatives, boards, brands, creator profiles, and organic discovery.

Today: competitor creatives and competitor brand context via Motion CLI. Coming soon/currently being wired: InSpo brands, unique creatives, boards, creators, TikTok organic posts, board contents, and board write flows.

primitives.label: Apps
primitives.tagline: Openable pages, dashboards, widgets, and previews Runneth creates.
primitives.summary: Use this for generated apps, openable links, dashboards, status pages, widgets, data-file-backed pages, app refreshes, and app visibility or auth issues.
productFeatures: Creates openable pages for reports, dashboards, previews, and internal tools.
Reads app data from files Runneth writes.
Can be refreshed when Runneth reruns the underlying data or build step.
userControls: What app Runneth should create or refresh.
Which source files or data files the app reads.
Whether the app should stay internal or be shared more broadly.

primitives.label: Routines
primitives.tagline: Scheduled, recurring, monitored, or later work.
primitives.summary: Use this for anything that creates, schedules, monitors, reminds, posts later, repeats, keeps work updated, refreshes an app on a cadence, or otherwise runs in the future.
productFeatures: Future, recurring, monitored, scheduled, or background work.
Routine planning and saved routine notes.
Best-effort deterministic refresh jobs only when explicitly allowed and exactly specified.
userControls: What the routine should do.
The cadence, trigger, or condition.
The destination or artifact to refresh, such as a Slack thread, app page, or data file.

thingsToKnow.detail: The status page should have a morning refresh routine that updates the page from repo state, relevant Linear tickets, and codebase-derived current state.
